Okay so this is a hard one... I do genuinely like this game, but I cannot recommend it unless it meets 1 single criteria: You care about the story of Titus.

I bought this game while it was on sale, had a good amount of fun in the waves game mode, but primarily played for the story of Titus (having played Space Marine 2 first).

The multiplayer is significantly dead, and that's the only thing there really is for you after the campaign. Maybe if you have a few friends also wanting to play an older shooter like this it's worth it, but by yourself, I can only say buy it if you're specifically looking for the story of Titus, as the second game's combat loop and mechanics are 100x cleaner and more engaging.

The one thing I can give this game over SM2 however is that the guns feel better in this game.

Good game, just unfortunately outdated by it's sequel and with a very inactive multiplayer scene. Try to get it on sale if you can.

My first Wahammer game.

So yeah, it's another Gears of War clone but without a cover system. You fight Orks for 80 percent of the game and then palette swaps of Space Marines and Demons for the rest. Makes you kind of miss the Orks.

I think the camera sucks and there's lots of samey environments. You go up the same elevators and walk down the same corridors a bunch of times. 

This game is really janky but it's never boring and yeah despite all my gripes with the game I really liked it.

Warhammer 40,000: Space Marine is a game that perfectly exemplifies 2011 era gaming.

Let me start by saying that I can absolutely see why the game was popular when it first released. The game’s main focus, making you feel like an unstoppable force for the Imperium , is executed wonderfully. Whenever you enter an area packed with enemies and start mowing them down, the gameplay feels perfectly suited for it.

Unfortunately, those exciting combat sections are separated by long stretches of running through empty hallways and waiting on elevators with nothing to do. I swear half my playtime was spent sprinting through barren corridors. Then, midway through the game, several enemy types are introduced that drain the fun out of the combat entirely, mainly the rocket enemies and the demons. The UI has also aged poorly, as have the clunky controls.

That’s enough about the negatives, though, so what does the game do well? I love games that throw you directly into their worlds instead of burying you under pages of exposition. The approach here is very much, “Here’s our universe, go look things up yourself if you want to learn more.” The weapons all feel fantastic, and around halfway through the game there are some genuinely tough decisions about which ones to carry.

The story itself is extremely barebones: protect this target, move this item from point A to point B, then take it back to point A and use it there. After that, go finish off the enemies. That’s pretty much the entire plot.

Overall, the game probably would have earned a much higher score from me if I had played it back in 2011, but today it mostly feels like a relic of its era. And that’s not even mentioning the constant crashing issues that both I and many other players experienced. I literally had to download a random file linked in a YouTube video and add it to the game’s files just to get it to launch.

All in all, I’d give the game a 4/10. I’d only recommend playing it if you want more background on the universe before jumping into Space Marine 2.

Despite its age, the game still feels fantastic, honestly even better than Space Marine 2 for the first few hours. The combat is fun, the pace is great, and it really nails the Warhammer feel early on.

Unfortunately, around the 4–5 hour mark, the campaign takes a noticeable turn for the worse. The game starts heavily punishing melee play and executions, often resulting in insta-deaths mid-animation. On top of that, you’re constantly bombarded by endless rockets and bomb squigs that keep spawning and rushing you between groups of Orks.

What starts as a great action experience slowly turns into something repetitive, chaotic, and frankly frustrating.
